compiler: Apple Swift 6.3.3, Swift language mode 5, optimized arm64 with assertions enabled
status: Unreleased working tree; final production queue budget is 128 MiB of estimated pending payload
method: Warm local Documents tree; filesystem caches were not cleared. All runs use fresh processes and empty private /tmp caches outside the scanned root.
Same compiled core selects serial or async using an ORBIT_TESTING flag. Serial includes the prior unreleased fresh-small-folder transaction optimization.
Each final phase orders variants serial, async, async, serial. Builds, tests and source edits stopped during each phase.

Core observes first nonempty preview and first preview after discovery. Model uses actual DiskModel periodic previews and automatic filename-cache preparation, excluding SwiftUI rendering, user settings, production caches and volume discovery.

Final app first_full_visible_seconds requires the expected final root file count, finished discovery and zero deferred directories. Serial full-visible is only sampled at final completion, so it is not a separately measured earliest full-preview baseline.
The telemetry search counters are uninstrumented zeros, not evidence that search preparation did no work.

Final 128-* samples are authoritative for the shipped default; final-* samples are the earlier 64 MiB experiment. Preliminary runs differ in traversal implementation and corpus and must not be pooled.
These small warm samples do not establish cold or whole-Mac performance. Timer outliers occurred in both variants and are preserved; this is not a rendering/frame-rate benchmark.

async_suite: PASS: secure cursor validates cached ancestors/root, rejects symlinks, bounds deep traversal and closes independent descriptors
PASS: fresh native mappings select async; fallback mappings retain the serial path
PASS: nested memory navigation, exact search, removal identity, commit retirement and metadata parity
PASS: pinned snapshots retain queued rows, newer snapshots filter them, and cancellation rejects stale reads
PASS: committed watermark preserves allocated totals before deferred hardlink accounting
PASS: removal preserves unrelated RAM navigation/search before writes and keeps the replacement inode after reconciliation
PASS: concurrent directory replacement rejects stale queued metadata and relists safely
PASS: denied and missing first directories retain unrelated discovery and RAM progress
PASS: within-batch and cross-batch duplicate names are rejected before exposure and repaired without losing unrelated RAM
PASS: byte-bounded backpressure and cancellation without a running writer
PASS: bounded directory frontier leaves durable work for serial continuation
PASS: SIGKILL before writes and after commit resumes pending directory work without loss
PASS: asynchronous discovery and durable mapping checks
notes: The first scratch runner used /private/tmp for a fixture whose gate compares against standardized /tmp. Correcting the runner path restored the unchanged preview-core check.
An earlier preview-model deadline failed during overlapping compilation, then passed in isolated diagnostics and subsequent full runs. No cause was proven.
Existing deterministic writer-pause/fallback fixtures explicitly opt out of independent discovery; the new suite separately verifies concurrent discovery and RAM-only actions.
